verdicts.reason: Quote states IP owns constraints of those crossings; ownership, not verifiable in sim.
Quote states SoC owns clocks and I/O delays, not specified by IP.
Meta statement about the document text, nothing to verify or exercise.

Clock definitions are SoC-owned timing constraints; asynchronous relationship with free frequency is exercisable in simulation by running independent clock ratios, so scenario is fine, but it is a stimulus condition not a MUST on the design. Strength should be MAY (free, no restriction).
Statement that no case analysis is required; nothing to verify, and MUST_NOT is a misreading.
Quote says 0.9 x period as the value; bound is a set_max_delay value, not simulation checkable. Rationale says bound shorter than one period; keep MUST. Wording 'must be 0.9' is acceptable.
Quote states EXC-002 with 0.9 x i_clk_rd period.
Quote gives 1 x i_clk_rd period and says bound is at most one period; the rule's 'at most 1x' is consistent.

Static configuration (not changed while FIFO in use) is a usage restriction on the environment: the inputs must not change while in use. Exercisable as a scenario; the false_path itself is not simulation checkable. Strength MUST_NOT on changing, actor master.
Quote states EXC-005 with 0.9 x i_clk_wr.
Quote states EXC-006 with 0.9 x i_clk_rd.
Quote prohibits whole-domain false path or unqualified clock groups.
Quote states conditional requirement; condition is garbled in the text but the quote supports it.
Descriptive of macro views being supplied at integration; no verifiable requirement.
Quote states dont_touch applied to synchronizer instances.
